item.title: Ep. 154 - Working With Suppliers - Part 1 [Business 300]
item.description:
You need your vendors and suppliers in order to serve your customers. If your care about your customers, you must care about your suppliers. They are there to help you deliver the value you've promised. And you need to approach them with that mindset.

They're not your employees. They are other business owners. Which means you are their customer.

You can help them understand what is valuable for you as their customer. You can help lay out the expectation to make their job of discovery easier.

There are 2 ways you do this.

item.title: Ep. 153 - Keep The Main Thing, The Main Thing [Business 300]
item.description: In anything we do, we're tempted to get distracted and derailed off the tracks we're on. I keep talking about serving customers as being the main idea - the entire point - in business. Serving the customer is the point of everything else you're trying to do. Everything else depends on it. You want your employees, vendors, and yourself to win. But that happens in connection with your customers winning. You need to keep that focus on the customer. You need the keep the main thing, the main thing.
item.author: Philip Kulishov

item.title: Ep. 152 - Business is Boring [Business 300]
item.description:
Owning and managing a business has it's moments of euphoria. But a big part of business development is the gruesome, daily grind of simply doing the same thing every day. Results are what's exciting. Actions are boring.   A business owner does not spend his time in the realm of results. Results are the outcome of work. The work itself is what the business owner does. 

Results are an outcome of consistent action in the same direction. Are you bored because you have to do the same thing every day? Good. Lean in, and get ready for some exciting results. It's when we own the boredom, that things get exciting.

That's because business is boring.

item.title: Ep. 151 - You Or The Problem, Who Will fold? [Business 300]
item.description: What should you do when you're under continual pressure to fold? Consider the consequence. If you're tempted to fold, consider the consequence. Consider the consequence of 2 things. First, consider the consequence of folding. And second, consider the consequence of not folding. When tempted to fold, consider the consequence. Consider the consequence of folding. Consider the consequence of holding. And then decide: It's you or the problem. Who will fold?
